model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.note: Model identity is the actual runtime model of the evaluating session, taken from the session environment (claude-opus-5[1m], Opus 5 with 1M context), not the agent definition's template text, which names claude-fable-5.

issues_detected.description: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is false, yet the record's own subsets enrol participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, other dementias, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and substance use disorder. Cognitively impaired adults and people with serious mental illness are conventionally treated as vulnerable populations in human-subjects research. The boolean is defensible only under the reading that consent-capacity screening removes the vulnerability, which the special_protections text supports by requiring participants to be able to consent for themselves in English, but the flag as written contradicts the cohort composition stated elsewhere in the same record.
issues_detected.recommendation: Set at_risk_groups_included to true and let special_protections carry the consent-capacity screening, or add a note stating explicitly that the flag records residual vulnerability after screening rather than the diagnoses present in the cohort.

issues_detected.description: data_protection_impacts records an ethicist review of sensitive fields and a published memorandum justifying controlled access for raw voice, while its own source_caveats records that the healthsheet answers 'No' to whether an impact analysis on data subjects was conducted. The record does not resolve which is the operative claim.
issues_detected.recommendation: This is disclosed rather than hidden and is the correct handling of a source conflict. Consider stating which activity the consortium itself would call a data protection impact assessment, so a reader can tell whether a formal DPIA exists.

issues_detected.description: keywords carries only four terms (voice, health, biomarkers, bridge2ai). The rubric threshold is five or more, and the four present cover neither the methods (acoustic features, Parquet, BIDS, machine learning) nor the conditions (dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, depression, chronic cough) that the description and subsets document at length. Search recall for this record is far below what its own content would support.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add keywords drawn from the record's own subsets and preprocessing text: speech, respiratory sounds, voice disorders, neurodegenerative disease, psychiatric disorders, acoustic biomarkers, audiomics, machine learning, PhysioNet, BIDS.

issues_detected.description: The record carries no variables slot and no is_tabular flag, although it distributes tab-separated phenotype tables and states that each is paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name. The column-level metadata that the dictionaries hold is described but never expressed as structured variable entries with identifiers.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate variables with the phenotype table columns and their identifiers, at least for the demographics, confounders and enrollment instruments, and set is_tabular true for the phenotype and static-feature components.

issues_detected.description: Four award identifiers are recorded for one core NIH project (OT2OD032720, 3OT2OD032720-01S1, 1OT2OD032720-01, 3OT2OD032720-01S3). All four match the NIH activity-code pattern and all resolve to the same core award; the record states plainly that the sources differ and that each is recorded as its source gives it. This is a source-fidelity choice rather than a defect, but a consumer reading funders programmatically will see four grants where one exists.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the four as recorded and add a machine-readable marker of which is the core project number, so downstream aggregation does not quadruple-count the award.

issues_detected.description: The software that produced the release is documented under machine_annotation_tools and external_resources rather than under software_and_tools, which is absent. The information is complete, including b2aiprep version 3.0.0 and repository URLs with licenses, but a consumer querying the canonical slot finds nothing.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mirror the tool inventory into software_and_tools, keeping machine_annotation_tools for the annotation-specific claims about Whisper and the derived-feature extractors.

semantic_insights: The DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 uses the PhysioNet prefix, which is the correct registrar for a dataset whose page, publisher, citation and distribution URLs all resolve to physionet.org. The id, doi and page agree with each other and with the stated version 3.1.0.

Every minted internal identifier is a fragment on the record's own DOI (doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#org-usf, #subset-mood, #grant-ot2od032720, #files-phenotype), so affiliations, cohorts, grants and file collections are addressable without inventing an external namespace.

The human-subjects chain is complete and internally coherent: involves_human_subjects true, a named single IRB at the University of South Florida with subsite approvals through it, separately documented Canadian research ethics board approvals for institutions outside the US single-IRB process, prospective written consent with a documented withdrawal mechanism, and a Certificate of Confidentiality over the identifiable source data.

The deidentification method is appropriate to the data type and the record understands why. HIPAA Safe Harbor is supplemented by indirect-identifier removal, geographic generalisation to country, removal of free-speech transcripts, and withholding of raw waveforms on the stated ground that voice is inherently identifying and cannot be fully deidentified. The record also discloses that k-anonymity with k of two or more is not achieved, which is an unflattering fact a boilerplate record would omit.

Tiered access is described at the level a prospective user needs to act on: PhysioNet credentialing plus the Registered Access Agreement for the derived features, and a Data Access Request Form, DACO review and an institutionally signed Data Use and Transfer Agreement for raw audio through Synapse syn72370534.

Preprocessing parameters are specific enough to reproduce: 16 kHz monaural resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter, a 25 ms window with 10 ms hop and 400-point FFT, 60 Mel bins, 60 MFCCs, sparc at 50 Hz, torchaudio pitch over 80 to 500 Hz and sparc pitch over 50 to 550 Hz, phonetic posteriorgrams over 40 phoneme categories at 100 Hz.

The record distinguishes what the release contains from what the project holds. Raw audio, laryngoscopy imaging, brain imaging, spirometry and genomic data are named as collected but excluded, with the genomic arm attributed to a separate Toronto and Mount Sinai protocol.

known_biases uses five distinct BiasTypeEnum values (selection, sampling, representation, measurement, annotation) with a mechanism for each, and the measurement-bias entry makes the non-obvious observation that cohort membership is confounded with recording site and with the particular tablet device used there.

Version history is traced across six releases with per-version DOIs, a version-independent DOI, three errata and an explicit statement that version 1.1 files are no longer available, so a reader can tell which versions are still retrievable.

Source conflicts are surfaced rather than silently resolved: the Health Data Nexus versus MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology hosting discrepancy, the 10,000 versus 30,000 enrolment targets, the 61,937 recording count that the preferred v3.1.0 source does not carry, and the corrupted award strings in the documentation acknowledgements are each recorded with the reasoning for the value chosen.

The two award strings 3TF-OT2ActfOD032720Projectf01S1 and 3Tf-OTOD03272001S2 are correctly identified as corrupted renderings of the core award rather than being recorded as further grants, which is the right judgement on text damaged in extraction.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; citation carries RRID:SCR_007345
sub_elements.quality_note: The DOI matches the 10.XXXX pattern and the 10.13026 prefix is PhysioNet's, which is the registrar the page, publisher and distribution URLs all name, so the prefix is plausible and consistent. The id repeats the DOI in CURIE form and every internal identifier in the record is a fragment on it. The RRID appearing in the citation is PhysioNet's resource RRID rather than a dataset RRID and no rrid slot is populated, but the DOI alone satisfies the sub-element.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description of roughly 2,300 characters covering 833 adult participants at five North American sites, four disease cohorts plus controls, the acoustic task battery, the questionnaire instruments, the diagnostic gold standards, and the derived-feature composition of the public release
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout. The description names the individual acoustic tasks (Rainbow and Caterpillar passages, Cape-V sentences, diadochokinesis, word-colour Stroop), the validated instruments (VHI-10, PHQ-9, GAD-7, PANAS, MoCA), and the validation modalities (laryngoscopy, stroboscopy, spirometry, brain CT and MRI). It also states what the release excludes, namely raw waveforms, which is the fact most likely to surprise a prospective user.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [voice, health, biomarkers, bridge2ai]
sub_elements.quality_note: Four keywords, below the threshold of five, and the four are generic programme-level terms. None of the methods (acoustic features, Parquet, BIDS, machine learning), the conditions (dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, depression, airway stenosis, chronic cough) or the modalities (speech, respiratory sounds, cough) that the description and the five cohort subsets document at length appear here. The record's own content would support twenty defensible keywords, so this is a discoverability gap the rest of the record does not compensate for.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; file_collections with four entries carrying path values (features, metadata, phenotype, b2ai-voice-audio), collection_type values (processed_data, metadata, raw_data) and per-collection conforms_to
sub_elements.quality_note: The landing page is version-pinned rather than generic. The resources slot is absent, but file_collections supplies the hierarchical structure the sub-element asks for and does so at file granularity, naming the nine Parquet files individually and enumerating the phenotype subfolder tables down to instrument level.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: six entries with relationship_type values derives_from (Synapse syn72370534 raw audio), is_supplemented_by (pediatric dataset doi:10.13026/h995-bt35), three is_new_version_of entries (v3.0.0, v1.1, v1.0 on Health Data Nexus) and is_version_of (the version-independent doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42); subsets with seven entries
sub_elements.quality_note: No parent_datasets slot, but the relational structure is expressed through typed related_datasets links that cover derivation, versioning and the companion pediatric release, each with a resolvable target and a description. The seven subsets add the internal hierarchy, distinguishing the five participant cohorts from the three release components.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use with license_terms describing the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License and credentialed-user requirement; ip_restrictions.restrictions with four entries covering copyright, non-assertion of IP claims, downstream IP on derivative work, and the absence of third-party restrictions
sub_elements.quality_note: The access policy is stated at the level a user must satisfy to obtain the data, and the IP position is unusually complete: it covers what the user may not claim, what the user may claim on downstream discoveries, and the Fort Lauderdale Agreement commitment that licensing must not obstruct further research.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; other_compliance stating that no export controls apply, that the identifiable source data are covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality that must be asserted against subpoenas, that recipients must apply administrative, physical and technical safeguards, and that unauthorised disclosure must be notified within five business days
sub_elements.quality_note: All three fields are populated with values consistent with each other and with the sensitivity of the content. The Certificate of Confidentiality detail and the five-business-day breach notification obligation are operative terms rather than compliance boilerplate.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[].access_urls: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ for the Parquet and TSV components and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ for the controlled-access WAV audio; data_governance.access_review_process giving the full route for each tier
sub_elements.quality_note: No download_url slot, but the sub-element accepts platform access instructions and these are precise: PhysioNet registration, identity confirmation, credentialed status and the Registered Access Agreement for the features, and a Data Access Request Form, DACO review at DACO@b2ai-voice.org and an institutionally signed Data Use and Transfer Agreement before Synapse release for the audio.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: three entries naming Apache Parquet for the dense derived features and per-recording metadata, tab-separated values with paired JSON data dictionaries for static features, audio quality metrics and phenotype tables, and WAV organised to BIDS for the controlled-access audio
sub_elements.quality_note: Each format entry says which components use it and carries its own access URL, so the reader can tell that the Parquet and TSV files come from PhysioNet while the WAV files come from Synapse. The nine Parquet files are named individually under file_collections.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: six typed entries; external_resources: seven entries including b2aiprep at github.com/sensein/b2aiprep under Apache-2.0, senselab, the REDCap data dictionary archived at zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724, the documentation site docs.b2ai-voice.org archived at zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653, FHIR profiles for voice, the Interspeech 2024 protocol publication, and the Voice Scholars training programme
sub_elements.quality_note: Both slots are populated with resolvable targets. The external resources carry archival flags and licences per entry, and the record notes where the healthsheet answers 'NA' to persistence guarantees rather than asserting a guarantee the sources do not support.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats is populated with three formats each carrying an access_url, page links to the PhysioNet v3.1.0 landing page, and license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is general_research_use, so the datasets-shared condition is met
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Files are released under the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, with access limited to credentialed users who sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement... No fees are associated with these restrictions'; intended_uses.usage_notes: 'intended for commercial and non-commercial research purposes by authorized researchers'; collection_consents recording that consent does not restrict use to non-commercial purposes, a geographic location, a research type, genetic research, or method and algorithm development
sub_elements.quality_note: The licence is named and its permissions and prohibitions are both stated. What makes this strong rather than adequate is that the consent scope is traced through to the licence: the record establishes that commercial and algorithm-development use is permitted because the participants consented to it, not merely because the licence is silent.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination: distribution_formats populated with access URLs, PhysioNet landing page present, licence permits general research use
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats format entries naming Apache Parquet as 'an open-source column-oriented binary data file format', tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries, and WAV organised to BIDS; file_collections.conforms_to: 'Apache Parquet and tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries' and 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0'
sub_elements.quality_note: Every distributed format is an open standard and each is bound to the component that uses it. Character encoding is not stated anywhere, which is a real gap for the tab-separated tables given that the record documents free-text narrative fields being removed rather than transcoded, but the formats themselves are standardised and explicitly identified, which is the substance of the sub-element.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination: the release is distributed through PhysioNet under a licence permitting general research use
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0'; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; per-collection conforms_to on file_collections; instances carrying B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30, B2AI_TOPIC:4 and B2AI_TOPIC:36 CURIEs
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels: the datasheet's own schema, the data organisation standard with a pinned version, and ontology CURIEs on the instance entries. The BIDS version is given as v1.9.0 rather than as a bare standard name, which is what a reuser needs to validate against.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination: the phenotype and feature tables are distributed through PhysioNet under the registered-access licence
sub_elements.evidence: No variables slot. file_collections describes 'a matching JSON data dictionary sharing its file stem' and 'JSON data dictionary keyed by column name', and enumerates phenotype instruments (confounders, demographics, eighteen diagnosis tables, eligibility, enrollment_form, participant, thirteen questionnaire tables, seven task tables)
sub_elements.quality_note: The record tells a reader that column-level metadata exists and where to find it, but does not carry any of it. No variable is named with an identifier, a type, a permitted-value range or a description anywhere in the record, so a consumer cannot select a variable or plan an integration without first downloading the data dictionaries. Naming the tables is table-level, not variable-level, metadata.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: three use categories with examples and usage_notes; prohibited_uses: five prohibition_reason entries covering re-identification attempts, foreseeable harm or stigmatisation, IP-based obstruction of access, sale of the data, and contacting subjects without IRB approval and written provider approval; discouraged_uses: three entries covering hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustment and surveillance; existing_uses recording the Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon
sub_elements.quality_note: All four use slots are populated and each prohibition carries its reason rather than only its rule, so a user can tell which prohibitions follow from the consent, which from the transfer agreement and which from the consortium's open-science commitments. The discouraged uses name concrete misuse scenarios and say what harm each would cause.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: description (E1) states 'Version 3.1.0 contains data for 833 adult participants collected at five sites in North America' and 'Participants were recruited at high-volume expert clinics'; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes a tablet application administered to participants with REDCap clinical data entry; regulatory_restrictions (E2) sets confidentiality_level to restricted and hipaa_compliant to compliant, so both the human-subjects and the governance conditions are independently satisfied through fields outside E4
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research.irb_approval: 'The clinical study was submitted to and approved by the University of South Florida single IRB, with subsite IRBs approved through the single IRB process'; ethics_review_board: University of South Florida Institutional Review Board; ethical_reviews: two entries, the second naming the Canadian research ethics boards at Mount Sinai Hospital, The Hospital for Sick Children and the University of Toronto; data_protection_impacts describing an ethicist review of sensitive fields and a published memorandum justifying controlled access for raw voice
sub_elements.quality_note: involves_human_subjects is true and the IRB chain is fully populated, so the consistency expectation holds. The record goes past a single approval statement to explain the regulatory structure: a US single IRB with subsites approved through it, separate Canadian REB applications because those institutions fall outside the single-IRB process, copies filed back with the USF IRB, and a distinct Toronto and Mount Sinai protocol for the genomic arm that is not in this release. The one blemish is that data_protection_impacts records an ethics review while its own caveat records the healthsheet answering 'No' to whether an impact analysis was conducted.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination: E1 description names adult participants recruited at clinics, E8 collection_mechanisms describes participant-administered collection, and E2 regulatory_restrictions declares restricted confidentiality with HIPAA compliance
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers, of highly sensitive non-identifying elements, and of all raw voice data from the public release'; identifiers_removed listing eighteen categories from names and civic addresses through dates finer than years, biometric identifiers, state and province with only country retained, narrative text and free-speech transcripts; deidentification_details stating that 'The dataset does not achieve k-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two'
sub_elements.quality_note: A named method with an enumerated identifier list, which is what the sub-element asks for, plus the reasoning for each layer: direct identifiers because they reveal identity, indirect identifiers where combination with public data creates significant risk, and derived features withheld where the source audio was open-response. The explicit statement that k-anonymity is not achieved is the strongest signal here, because it is a disclosure against interest that a template-filling record would not produce.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination via E1 description, E8 collection_mechanisms and E2 regulatory_restrictions
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.reidentification_risk: 'Voice is inherently identifying and cannot be fully de-identified, so raw voice data was removed from the public release and is disseminated only under controlled access. K-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two is not achieved for the released tables'; privacy_techniques naming tiered dissemination, institutional retention of identifiable data, study identifiers in place of institutional ones, transcript review for identifying content or external voices, HTTPS transmission to HIPAA-compliant storage, and federated learning infrastructure; data_linkage describing participant_id and session_id linkage with the key held at each site
sub_elements.quality_note: The risk assessment is specific to the modality rather than generic. It identifies why this data type resists deidentification, states the mitigation that follows from that fact, and then declines to claim a formal anonymity guarantee. The linkage description separates what links inside the release from the key that stays behind institutional controls, which is exactly the distinction a re-identification analysis turns on.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination via E1 description, E8 collection_mechanisms and E2 regulatory_restrictions
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type: 'Prospective written informed consent obtained before data collection'; consent_documentation covering paper, in-app electronic, REDCap survey and video-recorded consent with five-year retention; consent_scope covering EHR access for gold-standard validation, registered-access release of low-risk data and controlled-access release of higher-risk data; withdrawal_mechanism; consent_revocations recording that data cannot be removed once voice collection is complete
sub_elements.quality_note: The consistency expectation that human subjects implies documented consent is satisfied in full. The consent scope is mapped onto the actual release tiers rather than stated abstractly, and the withdrawal boundary is stated honestly: withdrawal before or during collection excludes the data, after completion it cannot be removed. The video-consent mechanism doubling as voice identity verification is a specific operational detail.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination via E1 description, E8 collection_mechanisms and E2 regulatory_restrictions
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: false with special_protections restricting the adult cohort to participants 18 or older able to read and speak English and to consent for themselves, and notes describing parental permission and verbal assent from about age seven for the separately published pediatric cohort; participant_compensation: electronic gift cards, 40 US dollars for a session under 90 minutes and 80 US dollars for one over 90 minutes, capped at three sessions and 120 US dollars total
sub_elements.quality_note: Compensation is documented to the level of amount, form and cap, which is what an ethics reviewer would check for undue inducement. Protections for the pediatric arm are described even though that cohort is released separately. The scored gap is the at_risk_groups_included boolean: the neurological cohort enrols participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias and the mood cohort enrols participants with schizophrenia and substance use disorder, so 'false' reads as inconsistent with the record's own subsets unless it is understood as residual vulnerability after consent-capacity screening. The sub-element still scores because both named fields carry substantive, actionable content.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subsets: five cohort entries with is_subpopulation true (Voice Disorders, Respiratory Disorders, Neurological and Neurodegenerative Disorders, Mood and Psychiatric Disorders, Control), each listing inclusion diagnoses, exclusion criteria and validation modality; subpopulations.identification naming age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status; subpopulations.distribution stating that the releases do not contain an equal distribution of cohort categories
sub_elements.quality_note: The cohort descriptions are clinical rather than nominal. The voice disorders entry enumerates laryngeal cancer staging, laryngitis subtypes, benign lesion types and dystonia variants, then lists the exclusions that most affect interpretation, such as previously treated cancer with no scope evidence and post-surgical patients within thirty days. The neurological entry gives the age window of over 44 and under 85. Only the distribution skew is qualitative; no per-cohort counts are given.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances[0].counts: 833 participants; instances[1].notes giving per-feature record counts (torchaudio pitch 32,522; sparc periodicity and pitch 31,872 each; sparc loudness 31,855; phonetic posteriorgrams 29,289; spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC 29,278 each; sparc electromagnetic articulography 28,640); version_access.version_details recording 12,523 recordings for 306 participants in the initial release; splits.split_details stating that no recommended splits are provided; subsets carrying is_data_split flags
sub_elements.quality_note: The participant count is exact and the recording counts are given per feature with the reason they differ, namely withheld sensitive records, withheld audio checks and files that could not be processed. The record declines to state an aggregate recording total and explains why in a source caveat: the documentation gives roughly 61,937 for version 3.0 but the preferred v3.1.0 source gives only per-feature counts. That is a better answer than reporting a figure the preferred source does not carry.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: No variables slot and no is_tabular flag. file_collections records 'Organized information collected from the participant or another individual during their encounter, as tab-separated tables each paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name' and lists the phenotype subfolder table names
sub_elements.quality_note: Both named fields are absent. The record establishes that the phenotype and static-feature components are tabular and that per-column dictionaries exist, but carries no column description, no variable identifier, no data type and no value range for any variable in the dataset. The instrument names (confounders.tsv, demographics.tsv, phq9, vhi10 and the rest) identify tables, not variables, so a reader cannot determine what a table contains without leaving the record.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances entries carrying data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:4 and B2AI_TOPIC:36 with data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41 and B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30; subsets enumerating the conditions covered, from laryngeal cancer, muscle tension dysphonia and unilateral vocal fold paralysis through airway stenosis and unexplained chronic cough to Alzheimer's disease, ALS, Parkinson's disease, anxiety, bipolar disorder and depression; label_description recording that labels follow Bridge2AI-Voice protocols and ICD-10 codes
sub_elements.quality_note: Topics are expressed both as ontology CURIEs on the instance entries and as an enumerated clinical vocabulary across the cohort subsets, with ICD-10 named as the coding system for the diagnostic labels. A reader can determine which conditions are represented and how they were coded.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: six entries covering differing site configurations and protocol change over the study, noise artifacts and varying microphone distance, inter-clinician diagnostic variation, questionnaire inaccuracy and underreporting, unaudited off-the-shelf models for derived text, and audio files that could not generate certain features; sampling_strategies with is_random false, is_representative false, why_not_representative and representative_verification; missing_data_documentation with missing_data_patterns, missing_data_causes and handling_strategy
sub_elements.quality_note: All three named field groups are populated substantively. The missing-data account is mechanistic rather than a count: rows appear only when at least one column is non-missing, cohort-specific instruments are systematically absent for participants outside that cohort, and feature files omit recordings that failed processing or were withheld. handling_strategy states that no imputation was performed and that a missingness table ships with the dataset.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated with PhysioNet and Synapse access URLs and a licence permitting general research use, so the datasets-shared condition is met
sub_elements.evidence: version: 3.1.0; page pinned to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; issued: '2026-05-01T00:00:00Z'
sub_elements.quality_note: A semantic version number that agrees with the pinned landing page URL, the issue date and the DOI recorded for that version in version_access.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination: the release is distributed through PhysioNet under the registered-access licence
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42; versions_available listing all six releases with dates and per-version DOIs where they exist; version_details: 'Each version of the dataset has a unique DOI and a version-independent DOI resolves to the latest version. By default older versions continue to be supported, hosted and made available to researchers... the files for version 1.1 are no longer available and users are directed to the latest version'
sub_elements.quality_note: The record distinguishes the version-independent DOI from the version-specific ones and states both the general retention policy and the exception to it. Telling a reader that v1.1 files are gone despite the stated policy is the kind of qualification that makes the rest of the block trustworthy.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination via distribution_formats, the PhysioNet landing page and the licence
sub_elements.evidence: errata: three entries covering the v2.0 spectrogram reprocessing and removal of free-speech-derived spectrograms and MFCCs, the v2.0.1 authorship correction, and the v3.1.0 repair of broken Parquet files; updates.update_details recording that v3.1.0 added no new participants but released additional data for certain participants, added audio quality metrics and per-recording metadata, back-filled validated diagnosis information, rearranged phenotype files and renamed gold standard variables
sub_elements.quality_note: Errata are per-version and specific about what changed. Each carries a source caveat recording that these come from the PhysioNet release notes and that the project states there is no separate erratum document, corrections being published in the per-version changelog instead, so the reader knows where the authoritative change record lives.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination via distribution_formats, the PhysioNet landing page and the licence
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: 'Semi-annual, that is twice a year'; updates.source_caveats: 'The semi-annual cadence is stated in the project documentation; the observed PhysioNet release dates run January 2025, April 2025, August 2025, December 2025 and May 2026'; updates.update_details describing notification through platform news items and a published changelog
sub_elements.quality_note: A stated cadence plus the observed release dates, which lets the reader check the claim rather than take it. The five observed dates are roughly four-monthly, so the record has surfaced a mild tension between the documented cadence and the actual one instead of relaying only the documented figure.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination via distribution_formats, the PhysioNet landing page and the licence
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: three entries covering the raw WAV waveforms with their Synapse access route, the REDCap-exported participant-reported responses, and the clinician validation records, each with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details; related_datasets.derives_from pointing at the Synapse raw audio; preprocessing_strategies recording assembly with b2aiprep version 3.0.0; distribution_dates listing six release dates
sub_elements.quality_note: No was_derived_from or release_notes slot, but raw_data_sources is one of the named fields and carries the full derivation chain: what the raw material was, in what format, who holds it now and how it can be reached. The record states plainly that the released features were derived computationally from the standardised audio using the b2aiprep pipeline at a pinned version, so the path from raw signal to distributed file is traceable.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: three entries covering the creation of a large ethically sourced diverse voice dataset linked to multimodal health biomarkers, the enabling of clinically applicable diagnostic models, and the standardisation of acoustic biomarkers as a field; addressing_gaps: four entries on prior small sample sizes and missing metadata, the absence of measurement standards preventing pooling, private industry datasets lacking clinical annotation and resisting audit, and the limited size, quality and diversity of existing open datasets
sub_elements.quality_note: Purpose and the gap it addresses are separated, and the gaps are argued rather than asserted. The point that industry holds large voice corpora that cannot be externally audited against gold-standard medical assessment is a specific research-landscape claim that motivates the ethically-sourced framing of the whole dataset.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: three entries covering training and evaluating disease detection and classification models with labels from vocal, neurological, psychiatric and respiratory categories; pretraining, fine-tuning, benchmarking and validating on the distributed derived features; and cohort selection and phenotypic analysis using the questionnaire, demographic, confounder and diagnosis tables
sub_elements.quality_note: The tasks are stated against the data that is actually released. The second and third both point at the derived features and phenotype tables rather than at the withheld raw audio, so the stated objectives are achievable with the registered-access files.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders.grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, through the Bridge2AI program'; maintainers entry with role government_agency recording NIH support via the Bridge2AI Common Fund programme; data_governance.notes repeating the NIH support
sub_elements.quality_note: The agency, the funding mechanism (Common Fund) and the programme (Bridge2AI) are all named, which is the level a funder-attribution consumer needs. The OT2 activity code on the awards is consistent with a Common Fund other-transaction award, so the mechanism and the grant numbers corroborate each other.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders.grants: OT2OD032720 with the full project title, the University of South Florida as awardee, Yael Bensoussan as PI and a 1 September 2022 to 30 November 2026 project period; 3OT2OD032720-01S1 cited in the PhysioNet v3.0.0 and v3.1.0 acknowledgements; 1OT2OD032720-01 from the feasibility publication funding statement; 3OT2OD032720-01S3 from NIH RePORTER application 11376382, fiscal year 2025, 4,660,942 US dollars
sub_elements.quality_note: All four identifiers match the NIH pattern of activity code, serial number, institute code (OD for the Office of the Director, correct for Common Fund) and digits, with supplement and year suffixes where present. Each is attributed to the source that gives it, and the record identifies the two corrupted strings in the documentation acknowledgements as damaged renderings of the same core award rather than recording them as additional grants.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: eighteen entries with principal_investigator names, affiliation identifiers minted on the dataset DOI, and CRediT credit_roles for those the sources support, plus a final entry recording that the PhysioNet author list names 117 further contributors and that the documentation credits over 50 investigators, clinicians, scholars and trainees; created_by naming the consortium and its two co-leads; citation carrying the full author list
sub_elements.quality_note: Roles are attributed to their evidence rather than assumed. Each PI carries a note on their project function (data acquisition module co-lead, mood disorders cohort lead, genomic data lead under a separate REB approval), and where CRediT roles were inferred from the IRB protocol and library authorship rather than from a CRediT statement, the entry says so in its own source caveat. The final entry prevents the eighteen named creators from reading as the full contributor list.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: collection fields are populated (acquisition_methods with four typed entries, collection_mechanisms with three) and the datasets-shared condition is met through distribution_formats, the PhysioNet access URLs and a licence permitting general research use
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: three entries naming the custom tablet application hosting the acquisition protocols, the recording hardware (iPad 9th or 10th generation and iPad Air 5th generation with an Avid AE-36 microphone through an Apple dongle, distinct devices per site), and REDCap for clinical, diagnostic and case report entry; collection_timeframes recording a 12-month collection period; data_collectors, direct_collection and collection_notifications
sub_elements.quality_note: The setting is described down to microphone model and tablet generation, and the record notes that distinct devices were used at each site, which it later connects to the measurement-bias entry. The timeframe entry states the 12-month duration and its caveat records that the healthsheet gives no calendar start or end dates, so the limit of the evidence is visible.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination: collection fields populated and the release distributed through PhysioNet under the registered-access licence
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: four entries with typed booleans, was_directly_observed for the supervised tablet recording with head-mounted headset microphone, was_reported_by_subjects for demographics, confounders and questionnaires, was_validated_verified for clinician diagnosis against per-cohort gold standards, and was_inferred_derived for the features computed from standardised audio with b2aiprep; raw_data_sources with three entries
sub_elements.quality_note: Each acquisition mode is flagged with the correct boolean and described, so a consumer can tell which parts of the dataset are observation, which are self-report, which are clinical adjudication and which are computed. The derived flag correctly marks every distributed feature as inferred rather than observed, which matters for anyone treating the features as measurements.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: external_resources (E10) references code repositories at https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, https://github.com/sensein/senselab, https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap and https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs, and purposes (E7) names the creation of bioinformatics standards for acoustic data as a project output, so the software-output condition is satisfied through fields outside E8
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: six entries giving 16 kHz monaural resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter, STFT with a 25 ms window, 10 ms hop and 400-point FFT with two-fold time downsampling, 60 Mel bins and 60 MFCCs, sparc at 50 Hz over six articulators, torchaudio pitch over 80 to 500 Hz and sparc pitch over 50 to 550 Hz, openSMILE and Parselmouth or Praat features, 40-category phonetic posteriorgrams at 100 Hz, the deidentification pass, and BIDS v1.9.0 conversion assembled with b2aiprep 3.0.0; cleaning_strategies: two entries; labeling_strategies with annotations_per_item 1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_platform, data_annotation_protocol and inter_annotator_agreement; machine_annotation_tools with tool_accuracy
sub_elements.quality_note: The preprocessing parameters are at reproduction level, and one entry carries a source caveat recording that v1.1 used a 512-point FFT without time downsampling, so a reader comparing versions is warned. The cleaning entries make the unusual admission that no cleaning preprocessing was applied and that an audit protocol runs instead, then describe that protocol. inter_annotator_agreement states honestly that a single labeller means no agreement statistic exists. No imputation_protocols slot, but missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy records that no imputation was performed, which is the substantive answer.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination: E10 external_resources names four code repositories and E7 purposes identifies bioinformatics standards for acoustic data as a project output
sub_elements.evidence: machine_annotation_tools.tools: OpenAI Whisper Large, openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, torchaudio, Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc), ppgs, b2aiprep, senselab, with tool_descriptions saying what each produced and tool_accuracy warning that off-the-shelf models such as the transcriber have not been audited for correctness; external_resources giving repository URLs with Apache-2.0 and MIT licences and Zenodo archives; preprocessing_strategies pinning b2aiprep to version 3.0.0
sub_elements.quality_note: The software_and_tools slot is absent, so the inventory sits in machine_annotation_tools and external_resources instead. The information the sub-element asks for is nonetheless complete: nine tools named, each mapped to the artefact it produced, repositories linked with licences and archival DOIs, and the pipeline library pinned to a version. The accuracy caveat on unaudited models is a quality statement most records omit.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination: the release is distributed through PhysioNet under a licence permitting general research use
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: seven entries including the Interspeech 2024 protocol development publication at isca-archive.org, the FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker, the REDCap data dictionary archived at Zenodo, the documentation site and its archived source, and the Voice Scholars training programme; conforms_to: BIDS v1.9.0; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]
sub_elements.quality_note: Standards and resources are both covered, with archival status and licence recorded per entry and Zenodo archival DOIs where they exist. The record states where the healthsheet answers 'NA' on persistence guarantees rather than asserting durability the sources do not support.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: six typed entries, coverage_limitation for English-only collection with Spanish protocols still in development, representativeness_limitation for the five North American sites, temporal_limitation for diagnostic practice change over the collection period, scope_limitation for the withheld raw waveforms and the features suppressed for sensitive records and free speech, integration_limitation for the laryngoscopy, brain imaging, respiratory function, genomic and EHR data extracted at sites but excluded, and methodological_limitation citing the AI-readiness self-assessment recording data quality as not met
sub_elements.quality_note: Each limitation carries a typed category and says what analysis it blocks rather than merely naming a shortcoming. The scope entry is the most useful, because it tells a reader precisely which analyses cannot be performed on the registered-access files: anything needing the original signal, and anything needing acoustic detail from open-response speech.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: five entries using BiasTypeEnum values selection_bias, sampling_bias, representation_bias, measurement_bias and annotation_bias, each with a bias_description, three with mitigation_strategy and two with affected_subsets; future_use_impacts recording that models trained without accounting for the skews risk unfair treatment of groups and quality-of-service harms
sub_elements.quality_note: Five distinct taxonomy values with a stated mechanism for each rather than a repeated observation. The measurement-bias entry identifies that participants were screened for different disorders by site so cohort membership is confounded with recording site and tablet device, and the representation entry notes that groups with less trust in the medical system or in AI were less likely to be recruited. future_use_impacts supplies the anticipated downstream social impact the sub-element asks for.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: six entries covering varying site configurations and protocol change during the study, noise artifacts and variable microphone distance from the head-mounted headset, inter-clinician and inter-site diagnostic variation, questionnaire inaccuracy and underreporting, unaudited off-the-shelf transcription models, and audio files that could not generate certain derived features
sub_elements.quality_note: The anomalies are causally specific and each is traceable to a mechanism described elsewhere in the record: the microphone distance to the collection_mechanisms hardware entry, the failed feature generation to the per-feature record count differences under instances, and the unaudited models to the tool_accuracy warning.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: four entries covering race and ethnicity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health information including psychiatric history and depression, anxiety, PTSD and ADHD questionnaire responses, and raw voice as biometric data; content_warnings with content_warnings_present true and a warning that free-speech tasks were open-response so offensive or distressing content cannot be entirely excluded; confidential_elements recording no legally privileged material
sub_elements.quality_note: Sensitive categories are enumerated individually rather than lumped, and the biometric-identifiability of voice is treated as a sensitive element in its own right, which ties directly to the controlled-access decision. The content warning carries a caveat noting that the released files exclude free-speech transcripts and free-speech-derived spectrogram features, so the residual exposure is limited to static features, which correctly scopes the warning to what a user of this release would actually encounter.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries, the first for the USF single IRB with subsite approvals and the note that the study is not for a drug product or medical device and that no data monitoring committee was appointed, the second for the Canadian research ethics boards with the explanation that Canadian institutions fall outside the US single-IRB process and filed copies of their approved applications with the USF IRB; data_protection_impacts recording the ethicist review and the controlled-access memorandum
sub_elements.quality_note: The review documentation is substantive and explains the regulatory structure rather than asserting an approval. Conflicts of interest are not addressed anywhere in the record, which is a genuine gap in the sub-element's secondary purpose, but the primary review documentation is complete, includes the negative findings (no drug or device, no data monitoring committee) and traces the separate genomic protocol to the institutions that approved it.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats carries PhysioNet and Synapse access URLs, page links the v3.1.0 landing page, and the licence permits general research use, so the datasets-shared condition is met
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://physionet.org; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; maintainers recording that PhysioNet is maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology; related_datasets and version_access recording the earlier Health Data Nexus release
sub_elements.quality_note: PhysioNet is a recognised repository for clinical physiological data and the publisher, page, DOI prefix and citation all agree on it. The maintainers entry carries a source caveat explaining that the documentation's Health Data Nexus hosting description corresponds to the earlier v1.0 release, so a hosting discrepancy across sources is resolved with a stated reason rather than left as a contradiction.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: external_resources names the Interspeech 2024 protocol development publication and the citation slot carries a formal dataset citation, so the publication condition is met, and the datasets-shared condition is met as above
sub_elements.evidence: citation: 'Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; version_access.latest_version_doi for the version-independent DOI
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete PhysioNet-format citation with author list, year, versioned title, publisher, RRID and resolvable DOI. The version stated in the citation matches the version slot and the landing page, and the version-independent DOI is offered separately for readers who want the latest release.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination: the release is distributed through PhysioNet under a licence permitting general research use
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0'; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; file_collections carrying per-collection conforms_to; external_resources naming FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker published by the consortium
sub_elements.quality_note: BIDS is pinned to a version, the datasheet declares its own schema and class, and the FHIR profile work shows the project contributing standards rather than only consuming them. The B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs on the instance entries add ontology-level conformance.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination: the release is distributed through PhysioNet under a licence permitting general research use
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources including the project documentation site and dashboards at https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/ with source at github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs archived at Zenodo, the Bridge2AI Voice Scholars training programme at https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/, the Interspeech 2024 protocol publication, and the b2aiprep and senselab repositories; extension_mechanism.contribution_url pointing at the b2aiprep repository with a description of the discussion forums, issue pages and pull request route
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation, training and contribution routes are all present. The Voice Scholars programme is a genuine outreach resource rather than a documentation link, and the extension mechanism tells a would-be contributor exactly where to raise an issue or submit a change to the preprocessing code.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same determination: the release is distributed through PhysioNet under a licence permitting general research use
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: six entries with relationship_type values derives_from, is_supplemented_by, is_new_version_of (three) and is_version_of, targeting the Synapse raw audio collection, the pediatric dataset doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 with its 23,533 recordings from 300 participants aged 2 to 18 at The Hospital for Sick Children, versions 3.0.0, 1.1 and 1.0, and the version-independent DOI
sub_elements.quality_note: Every relationship is typed and every target resolves. The pediatric dataset is correctly related through is_supplemented_by rather than absorbed into this dataset's own distribution, which is the distinction the project's scope declaration turns on, and its description makes clear that it is a separate release with its own participants and age range.

strengths: The ethics chain is complete and internally coherent from end to end: human subjects declared, a named single IRB with subsite approvals through it, separately documented Canadian research ethics board approvals for institutions outside the US single-IRB process, prospective written consent with four documented recording modes, a stated withdrawal boundary, a Certificate of Confidentiality over identifiable source data, and compensation given as amounts with a per-participant cap.

Deidentification is treated as a reasoning problem rather than a checkbox. HIPAA Safe Harbor is supplemented by indirect-identifier removal with the stated criterion of significant re-identification risk through combination with public data, geographic generalisation to country, transcript review, and withholding of raw waveforms on the ground that voice is inherently identifying. The record then discloses that k-anonymity with k of two or more is not achieved, a fact against interest that a template-driven record would omit.

Preprocessing is documented at reproduction level: 16 kHz monaural resampling with a Butterworth filter, a 25 ms window with 10 ms hop and 400-point FFT, 60 Mel bins, 60 MFCCs, sparc at 50 Hz over six articulators, pitch ranges of 80 to 500 Hz and 50 to 550 Hz for the two estimators, 40-category posteriorgrams at 100 Hz, and assembly with b2aiprep pinned to version 3.0.0, with a caveat recording where the v1.1 parameters differed.

Source conflicts are surfaced and adjudicated with stated reasons rather than silently resolved. The Health Data Nexus versus MIT hosting discrepancy, the 10,000 versus 30,000 enrolment targets, the 61,937 recording total the preferred source does not carry, the corrupted award strings, and the healthsheet's 'No' on impact analysis are each recorded with the evidence and the choice made.

Bias and limitation disclosure is mechanistic and self-consistent. Five distinct taxonomy values each carry a causal account, and the observations connect across the record: differing tablet devices per site appear under collection mechanisms, again as an anomaly, and again as the confound behind the measurement-bias entry.

Version tracking covers six releases with per-version DOIs, three errata, a version-independent DOI, an observed release-date sequence that lets the reader check the stated semi-annual cadence, and an explicit statement that v1.1 files are no longer retrievable despite the general retention policy.

The distinction between what the project holds and what this release distributes is maintained throughout: raw audio, laryngoscopy and brain imaging, spirometry, genomic data and other EHR content are each named as collected and each excluded, with the genomic arm attributed to its own separate Toronto and Mount Sinai protocol.
weaknesses: keywords carries only four generic terms, below the rubric threshold of five and far below what the record's own content supports. None of the modalities, methods or clinical conditions documented at length in the description and the five cohort subsets are indexed, so discoverability is the weakest property of an otherwise thorough record.

No variables slot anywhere in the record. The phenotype tables and their per-column JSON data dictionaries are described and the instrument-level table names are enumerated, but no single variable is given with an identifier, type, permitted values or description, so a consumer cannot select or integrate a variable without downloading the data first. This costs the record two separate sub-elements.
No is_tabular flag, despite the release distributing tab-separated phenotype tables, a static feature table and audio quality metrics as its principal structured components.

at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is false while the record's own subsets enrol participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, other dementias, schizophrenia and substance use disorder. The consent-capacity screening described in special_protections makes the flag defensible, but nothing in the record says that is what the flag means.
Character encoding is not stated for the tab-separated tables, which matters for a dataset that documents removing narrative text fields rather than transcoding them.
Conflicts of interest are not addressed anywhere, although the ethical review documentation is otherwise complete.

The software inventory sits under machine_annotation_tools and external_resources rather than software_and_tools, which is absent, so a consumer querying the canonical slot finds nothing even though the information is complete.
recommendations: Expand keywords from four to at least twelve, drawing directly from the record's own subsets and preprocessing text: speech, respiratory sounds, cough, voice disorders, dysphonia, neurodegenerative disease, Parkinson's disease, psychiatric disorders, depression, acoustic biomarkers, audiomics, machine learning, PhysioNet, BIDS, Parquet.

Populate variables with the columns of at least the demographics, confounders and enrollment instruments, giving each an identifier, a type and a description, and set is_tabular true for the phenotype and static-feature components. This is the single change that would recover both lost sub-elements.

Either set at_risk_groups_included to true and let special_protections carry the consent-capacity screening, or add a note stating that the flag records residual vulnerability after screening rather than the diagnoses present in the cohort.
State the character encoding of the tab-separated phenotype and feature tables, and add encoding to the distribution format entries.
Add a conflict-of-interest statement to ethical_reviews, or record explicitly that the sources contain none, so the absence is a finding rather than a gap.
Mirror the tool inventory into software_and_tools with versions where known, keeping machine_annotation_tools for the annotation-specific claims about Whisper and the derived-feature extractors.
State which of the four recorded award identifiers is the core project number, so downstream funder aggregation does not read one award as four.
